pageDescription: Live system resource monitoring with per-process breakdown
endProcessDescription: This will forcefully terminate {{name}} (PID {{pid}}). Unsaved data in this application may be lost.
diskHealthAdminHint: Run as Administrator for detailed S.M.A.R.T. data
cpuHighAlert: CPU usage is critically high (>90% sustained)

apps.title: App resource usage
apps.search: Search app, path, user or PID...
apps.groupingHelp: Grouped by executable and user where available. Different helper executables can appear separately. Switch to Processes to end an individual process.
apps.estimatedHelp: Approximate group: the OS did not expose an executable path or account for every process. Same-named executables or different accounts may be combined.
apps.trendHelp: Session-only trend, up to the selected time range (15 minutes maximum). Requires 30 seconds of samples. Includes processes starting or stopping; growth alone does not prove a leak. Resets after a sampling gap or app restart.
apps.parentHelp: Parent links are shown only when both start times can be verified. A missing parent or reused PID is not treated as a process tree.
apps.paused: Paused | showing the last collected values
apps.failed: Process sampling failed | previous values may be stale. Sampling will retry automatically.
apps.stale: Updates delayed | showing the last collected values
apps.empty: No process data was returned by the operating system.
apps.caveat: Working set is resident memory summed across observed processes. Shared pages can be counted more than once, so app totals will not add up to system RAM usage. All observed processes are included before sorting or filtering.
apps.identityUnavailable: End Process is unavailable because the operating system did not expose a stable creation identity.

memoryContext.title: Memory context
memoryContext.sampled: Windows memory counters | sampled about every 10s
memoryContext.windowsOnly: Commit and paging counters are available on Windows only.
memoryContext.explanation: High RAM use alone does not mean memory pressure. Compare available RAM, commit headroom and sustained paging with actual slowdowns. Commit is memory Windows promises to back with RAM or page files, not page-file usage. Pages read can include executable and mapped files as well as page files, so a brief spike is not proof of insufficient RAM. Working-set growth can reflect normal caching or new app processes. Close unused tabs or save work and quit an app normally before considering End Process.
memoryContext.lastAvailable: Last observed available RAM | paused or stale
